_source: Ministry of Education / Curriculum Development Centre, Zambia. 'Chemistry Syllabus (5070), Grade 10-12' (2013, published by CDC) — Grade 10, Topics 10.1-10.4. Topic, sub-topic and Specific Outcome statements only; the 'Content' (Knowledge/Skills/Values) columns are omitted, consistent with the approach used for the other 2013 OBC subjects in this app. This document's outcome numbering is reliable and matches its sub-topic structure. One outcome (10.4.2.11) is split awkwardly across a page break in the source PDF's text extraction ('Identify the...' followed on the next page by 'differences in properties of ionic and covalent compounds'); it is reproduced here as the single joined sentence it clearly is. The syllabus organizes content by Grade only, not by Term, so all of Grade 10 is modeled as a single term here. STRUCTURAL TERM SPLIT (2026-08-31, not sourced): this file's topics were previously modeled as a single undivided 'Year' block (no real per-topic term/week data exists for this subject/grade). At the user's own explicit request and choice among alternatives offered, the SAME real topics above have now been divided into three roughly-equal-by-content-volume groups, in their original curriculum order, labelled 'Term 1'/'Term 2'/'Term 3' purely so the app can generate and share one term at a time. This division of which topic falls in which term is NOT sourced from any real scheme of work - it is an organizational split only. No topic, sub-topic, competency, or objective was added, removed, or altered; only the grouping changed. Each term's own topics still have no real week_number of their own, so within a term the app's existing calendar-pacing engine spreads them algorithmically across that term's real teaching weeks, exactly as it already did for the whole undivided Year block before this split. UPDATE (2026-09-02): two real Ministry of General Education 'Grade 10 Pure Chemistry Common Scheme of Work' documents (Term 1 and Term 2, 2018 - shared with this app's Drive account; no individual name in either, nothing to sanitize) confirm the real term placement for three of this file's four topics, matched by content against this file's own reliable official sub-topic text: Term 1 covers Introduction to Chemistry and The Particulate Nature of Matter in full, plus only the 'Measuring of Quantities' sub-topic of Experimental Techniques; Term 2 covers the REST of Experimental Techniques - Criteria of Purity and Separating Mixtures - and nothing else. This is a genuine case where the real source splits a single topic's own sub-topics across two terms (Experimental Techniques' three sub-topics were previously kept together in one block by the earlier non-sourced split), so this update follows the real source rather than keeping them together. Atoms, Elements, Compounds and Molecules is not mentioned in either real document; by elimination (Term 1 and Term 2 are now fully accounted for by the other three topics) it is placed in Term 3 - that placement is this app's own inference from elimination, not itself directly sourced. No sub-topic, competency, or objective was added, removed, or altered anywhere in this update - only which term each topic (and, for Experimental Techniques, which term each of its sub-topics) belongs to.

competencies.description: Describe Chemistry
Classify the branches of chemistry
Explain the importance of chemistry
Describe the challenges of chemical industrial activities
Demonstrate an appreciation of safety in the laboratory
Describe matter
Classify the basic units of matter
Classify the states of matter
Illustrate changes of states of matter
Describe the absorption and release of heat during changes of states of matter
Describe diffusion
Demonstrate diffusion in fluids
Describe the factors that affect the rate of diffusion
Demonstrate how different quantities are measured
Identify different measuring apparatus used in chemistry
Identify various measuring instruments and other apparatus used in chemistry
Describe the differences between a pure substance and a mixture
Demonstrate how to determine the purity of a substance
Explain the importance of purity of a substance
Distinguish between physical and chemical changes
Demonstrate different methods of separating mixtures
Interpret simple paper chromatograms
Describe an atom and its structure
Describe the relative charges and approximate relative masses of protons, neutrons and electrons
Describe the proton (atomic) number and nucleon (mass) number and nuclide notation
Describe what an element is
Identify elements using their chemical symbols
Describe the basis of the Periodic Table
Describe what isotopes are
Calculate relative atomic mass of an element given the percentage abundances of isotopes and from a mass spectrum
Describe the use of radioactive isotopes
Demonstrate the build-up of electrons in shells
Describe what a compound is
Describe the formation of ions (radicals)
Describe the formation of ionic (electrovalent) bonds
Describe the formation of covalent bonds
Describe the electronic arrangement in simple multiple covalent molecules
Describe the uses of ionic and covalent compounds
Describe what a molecule is
Describe what valency and valence electrons are
Demonstrate how to deduce valency of an element
Formulate chemical formulae of compounds
Identify the differences in properties of ionic and covalent compounds
Describe metallic bonding
Describe the electrical/thermal conductivity of metals
Describe the giant covalent structures of graphite and diamond
Describe the uses of graphite and diamond in relation to their structures
Describe the macromolecular structure of silicon (IV) oxide (silicon dioxide)
Identify the similarities in properties between diamond and silicon dioxide
Demonstrate how to construct word equations
Formulate balanced chemical equations
Construct net ionic equations from balanced chemical equations
